source_text: «μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν, ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε.» Ὄλεθρος δὲ ἡ δίκη τοῖς ἀπ' αὐτοῦ παρέχουσιν ἀλλογενεῖ· «Μὴ δῶτε γὰρ,» φησὶ, «τὰ ἅγια τοῖς κυσὶ, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων.» Τὸ γάρ τοι προσάγειν ἀτημελῶς τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἔτι τὰ κεκρυμμένα, καὶ τὰ μόνοις ἁγίοις πρέποντα, κινδύνου μεστόν· ἁγιάζεται γὰρ οὐ τὸ βέβηλον ἔτι καὶ νοσοῦν ἐκτόπως τὴν ἀκαθαρσίαν, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἤδη κεκαθαρμένον διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Κατὰ τὸν ἴσον τουτονὶ τρόπον καὶ λόγον, τὴν τοῦ θυμιάματος ποιεῖσθαι κατασκευὴν διετύπου, λέγων· «Καὶ σὺ λάβε σεαυτῷ ἡδύσματα, στακτὴν καὶ ὄνυχα, καὶ χαλβάνην ἡδυσμοῦ, καὶ λίβανον διαφανῆ, ἴσον ἴσῳ ἐστὶν, καὶ ποιήσουσιν αὐτῷ θυμίαμα μυρεψικόν· ἔργον μυρεψοῦ μεμιγμένον, καθαρὸν, ἔργον ἅγιον. Καὶ συγκόψεις ἐκ τούτων λεπτῶς, καὶ θήσεις ἀπέναντι τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ὅθεν γνωσθήσομαί σοι ἐκεῖθεν. Ἅγιον τῶν ἁγίων ἔσται ὑμῖν θυμίαμα. Κατὰ τὴν σύνθεσιν ταύτην οὐ ποιηθήσεται ὑμῖν ἑαυτοῖς. Ἁγίασμα ἔσται ὑμῖν Κυρίῳ. Ὃς ἂν ποιήσῃ ὡσαύτως, ὥστε ὀσφραίνεσθαι ἐν αὐτῷ, ἀπολεῖται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ.» Ὑποφαίνει δὲ πάλιν ἡμῖν ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγος, ὅτι τὰ ἰδικῶς ἐξαίρετα τῆς ἁπασῶν ἐπέκεινα φύσεως. Μέτεστι μὲν τῶν πεποιημένων οὐδενὶ οὐσιωδῶς, κοινὸν δὲ τῇ κτίσει παντελῶς οὐδὲν, πρὸς τὸν ποιητὴν καὶ δεσπότην, τόγε ἧκον εἰς ἀξίας λόγον καὶ γερῶν ὑπεροχήν. Μεμνησόμεθα δὲ καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν, καὶ αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σύνθετον καὶ λεπτὸν θυμίαμα Χριστὸν εἰρηκότες, καὶ αὐτὸν ἡμῖν τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ δι' ἀμφοῖν σημαίνεσθαι. Οὐκοῦν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀναφερομένου τοῦ θυμιάματος (εὐῶδες γὰρ ἀσυγκρίτως), οὐ ποιήσομεν ἑαυτοῖς κατ' αὐτὸ δὴ τὸ θυμίαμα. Ἕτερον γὰρ ἐπ' αὐτῷ παντελῶς οὐδένα παραδεξόμεθα, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ οἱ τάλανες Ἰουδαῖοι, τὸν τῆς ἀνομίας υἱόν. Ἑαυτοῖς γὰρ οἱ τοιοίδε συνθέντες ἁλώσονται, καὶ κατ' ἐκεῖνο δὴ τὸ εὐῶδες καὶ ἐξαίρετον ἀληθῶς θυμίαμα, τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς, τοῦ τὴν μὲν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ πεφανερωκότος ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ, δι' οὗ καὶ ἡμεῖς εὐωδιάζομεν, οὐχ ἑαυτοῖς συνθέντες τὸ θυμίαμα τὸ λεπτὸν, ἀλλ' ὡς μέτοχοι τοῦ θυμιάματος, καὶ τῇ τοῦ Πνεύματος χάριτι κατακεχρισμένοι, καὶ διὰ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτείας εὐδοκιμεῖν σπουδάζοντες. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Διὰ παντὸς οὖν, ὡς ἔοικεν, τοῦ γεγονότος ἐν, τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, τὸ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῖν διαμορφοῦται μυστήριον. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ καταθαυμάσειας ἂν, εἰ μάθοις ὅτι καὶ αὐτοὶ τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς οἱ τεχνουργοὶ Χριστὸν διαπλάττουσιν, ὡς ἔν γε σφίσιν αὐτοῖς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τίνα φὴς τρόπον; ἐννοεῖν γὰρ οὐκ ἔχω. {ΚΥΡ.} Γέγραπται γὰρ αὖ· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἀνακέκλημαι ἐξ ὀνόματος τὸν Βεσελεὴλ τὸν τοῦ Οὐρίου υἱὸν, υἱοῦ Ὢρ τῆς φυ
pass_a_gloss: [Opens mid-quotation; «Patera gar, phēsi» stands at the end of §30.] '…mē kalesēte (do not call) [father] hymōn epi tēs gēs; for heis (one) is your Patēr, the one in the heavens, and all of you are adelphoi.' Olethros (destruction) is the dikē (penalty) for those parechousin (giving) ap' autou (from it, the oil) to an allogenēs (foreigner). For 'Mē dōte (do not give),' he says, 'ta hagia to the kysi (dogs), nor balēte your margaritas before the choirōn (swine).' For prosagein atēmelōs (to bring carelessly) to those apistois eti (still unbelieving) ta kekrymmena (the hidden things) and things preponta (fitting) only for the hagioi is kindynou meston (full of danger); for hagiazetai (is sanctified) not to bebēlon (the profane) still and nosoun ektopōs (sick extraordinarily) with akatharsia, but to ēdē kekatharmenon (the already cleansed) through holy baptisma. PALL.: Alēthes (true). CYR.: According to this isos (same) tropos and logos he dietypou (prescribed/patterned) the kataskeuē (preparation) of the thymiama (incense), saying: 'And you, take hēdysmata (sweet spices), staktē (stacte), onyx (onycha), chalbanē hēdysmou (galbanum of sweetness), libanos diaphanēs (transparent frankincense), ison isō (equal to equal), and they shall make it thymiama myrepsikon (perfumer's incense), ergon myrepsou (perfumer's work), memigmenon (mixed), katharon, ergon hagion. And synkopseis leptōs (beat finely) from these and thēseis (place) apenanti (before) the martyrion in the skēnē tou martyriou, whence gnōsthēsomai soi (I will be made known to you). Hagion tōn hagiōn shall the incense be to you. By this synthesis (composition) it shall not be made for yourselves; hagiasma (a holy thing) to you for the Lord. Whoever makes likewise hōste osphrainesthai (so as to smell) in it apoleitai (shall perish) from his people.' The logos on this hypophainei (hints) again that ta idikōs exaireta (the specially reserved things) [belong] to the physis epekeina hapasōn (nature beyond all). They metesti (belong) to none of tōn pepoiēmenōn (things made) ousiōdōs (essentially), and koinon pantelōs ouden (nothing at all in common) has the ktisis with the poiētēs kai despotēs as regards logos axias (measure of dignity) and gerōn hyperochē (pre-eminence of honors). Memnēsometha (we will remember) having said the thysiastērion to chrysoun and the syntheton kai lepton thymiama itself [to be] Christ, and Emmanuel himself sēmainesthai (to be signified) di' amphoin (through both). Therefore the incense anapheromenou (being referred) to Christ (euōdes asynkritōs, fragrant incomparably), we shall not poiēsomen (make) for ourselves kat' auto (according to it) incense. For heteron (another) ep' autō (besides/over him) pantelōs oudena paradexometha (we shall receive none at all), kathaper amelei (just as indeed) the talanes (wretched) Jews [will receive] ton tēs anomias hyion (the son of lawlessness). For such synthentes heautois (having compounded for themselves) halōsontai (will be caught), even after that euōdes and exaireton (special) incense of God and Father, who pephanerōkotos (has manifested) to us the osmē tēs gnōseōs autou (smell of his knowledge) en tō Hyiō, through whom we too euōdiazomen (are fragrant), not having compounded the lepton incense for ourselves, but as metochoi (sharers) of the incense, katakechrismenoi (anointed) with the charis of the Pneuma, and spoudazontes (striving) eudokimein (to be approved) through the en Christō politeia (way of life in Christ). PALL.: Through everything gegonotos (made) in the hagia skēnē, hōs eoiken (as it seems), the mystērion of the Sōtēr diamorphoutai (is given form) for us. CYR.: And besides this katathaumaseias an (you would marvel) if you learned that even the technourgoi (craftsmen) of the holy tent themselves diaplattousin (fashion/portray) Christ, hōs en ge sphisin autois (in themselves at least). PALL.: Tina tropon (in what way) do you say? For ennoein ouk echō (I cannot conceive). CYR.: For it gegraptai again: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Idou, anakeklēmai ex onomatos (I have called by name) Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tri[be]…' [breaks mid-word at the column end].

Ὄλεθρος (destruction) is the δίκη (penalty) for those παρέχουσιν (giving) ἀπ' αὐτοῦ (from it, the oil) to an ἀλλογενής (foreigner). For 'Μὴ δῶτε (do not give),' he says, 'τὰ ἅγια to the κυσί (dogs), nor βάλητε your μαργαρίτας before the χοίρων (swine).' For προσάγειν ἀτημελῶς (to bring carelessly) to those ἀπίστοις ἔτι (still unbelieving) τὰ κεκρυμμένα (the hidden things) and things πρέποντα (fitting) only for the ἅγιοι is κινδύνου μεστόν (full of danger); for ἁγιάζεται (is sanctified) not τὸ βέβηλον (the profane) still and νοσοῦν ἐκτόπως (sick extraordinarily) with ἀκαθαρσία, but τὸ ἤδη κεκαθαρμένον (the already cleansed) through holy βάπτισμα. PALL.: Ἀληθές (true). CYR.: According to this ἴσος (same) τρόπος and λόγος he διετύπου (prescribed/patterned) the κατασκευή (preparation) of the θυμίαμα (incense), saying: 'And you, take ἡδύσματα (sweet spices), στακτή (stacte), ὄνυξ (onycha), χαλβάνη ἡδυσμοῦ (galbanum of sweetness), λίβανος διαφανής (transparent frankincense), ἴσον ἴσῳ (equal to equal), and they shall make it θυμίαμα μυρεψικόν (perfumer's incense), ἔργον μυρεψοῦ (perfumer's work), μεμιγμένον (mixed), καθαρόν, ἔργον ἅγιον. And συγκόψεις λεπτῶς (beat finely) from these and θήσεις (place) ἀπέναντι (before) the μαρτύριον in the σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, whence γνωσθήσομαί σοι (I will be made known to you). Ἅγιον τῶν ἁγίων shall the incense be to you. By this σύνθεσις (composition) it shall not be made for yourselves; ἁγίασμα (a holy thing) to you for the Lord. Whoever makes likewise ὥστε ὀσφραίνεσθαι (so as to smell) in it ἀπολεῖται (shall perish) from his people.' The λόγος on this ὑποφαίνει (hints) again that τὰ ἰδικῶς ἐξαίρετα (the specially reserved things) [belong] to the φύσις ἐπέκεινα ἁπασῶν (nature beyond all). They μέτεστι (belong) to none of τῶν πεποιημένων (things made) οὐσιωδῶς (essentially), and κοινὸν παντελῶς οὐδέν (nothing at all in common) has the κτίσις with the ποιητὴς καὶ δεσπότης as regards λόγος ἀξίας (measure of dignity) and γερῶν ὑπεροχή (pre-eminence of honors). Μεμνησόμεθα (we will remember) having said the θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν and the σύνθετον καὶ λεπτὸν θυμίαμα itself [to be] Christ, and Emmanuel himself σημαίνεσθαι (to be signified) δι' ἀμφοῖν (through both). Therefore the incense ἀναφερομένου (being referred) to Christ (εὐῶδες ἀσυγκρίτως, fragrant incomparably), we shall not ποιήσομεν (make) for ourselves κατ' αὐτό (according to it) incense. For ἕτερον (another) ἐπ' αὐτῷ (besides/over him) παντελῶς οὐδένα παραδεξόμεθα (we shall receive none at all), καθάπερ ἀμέλει (just as indeed) the τάλανες (wretched) Jews [will receive] τὸν τῆς ἀνομίας υἱόν (the son of lawlessness). For such συνθέντες ἑαυτοῖς (having compounded for themselves) ἁλώσονται (will be caught), even after that εὐῶδες and ἐξαίρετον (special) incense of God and Father, who πεφανερωκότος (has manifested) to us the ὀσμή τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ (smell of his knowledge) ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ, through whom we too εὐωδιάζομεν (are fragrant), not having compounded the λεπτόν incense for ourselves, but as μέτοχοι (sharers) of the incense, κατακεχρισμένοι (anointed) with the χάρις of the Πνεῦμα, and σπουδάζοντες (striving) εὐδοκιμεῖν (to be approved) through the ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτεία (way of life in Christ). PALL.: Through everything γεγονότος (made) in the ἁγία σκηνή, ὡς ἔοικεν (as it seems), the μυστήριον of the Σωτήρ διαμορφοῦται (is given form) for us. CYR.: And besides this καταθαυμάσειας ἄν (you would marvel) if you learned that even the τεχνουργοί (craftsmen) of the holy tent themselves διαπλάττουσιν (fashion/portray) Christ, ὡς ἔν γε σφίσιν αὐτοῖς (in themselves at least). PALL.: Τίνα τρόπον (in what way) do you say? For ἐννοεῖν οὐκ ἔχω (I cannot conceive). CYR.: For it γέγραπται again: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Ἰδού, ἀνακέκλημαι ἐξ ὀνόματος (I have called by name) Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tri[be]…' [breaks mid-word at the column end].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …‘call no one on earth your father; for you have one Father, who is in heaven, and you are all brothers’ (Matthew 23:9, 8). And the penalty for those who give any of the oil to a foreigner is destruction (Exodus 30:33). For he says, ‘Do not give what is holy to the dogs, and do not throw your pearls before swine’ (Matthew 7:6). For to bring the hidden things, the things fit only for the holy, carelessly before those who are still unbelievers is full of danger. For what is sanctified is not what is still profane and grievously sick with uncleanness, but what has already been cleansed through holy baptism.

Cyril: In the same way and on the same principle he laid down how the incense was to be prepared, saying: ‘And you, take for yourself sweet spices, stacte and onycha, fragrant galbanum and clear frankincense, an equal weight of each, and they shall make of it a perfumed incense, the work of a perfumer, blended, pure, a holy work. And you shall beat some of it very fine and put it before the testimony in the tent of witness, where I will make myself known to you. The incense shall be most holy to you. You shall not make any for yourselves according to this composition; it shall be holy to you for the Lord. Whoever makes any like it, to smell it, shall perish from his people’ (Exodus 30:34–38). Here again the passage hints to us that the things specially reserved belong to the nature that is beyond all natures. None of the things that have been made has a share in them by essence, and creation has nothing whatever in common with its Maker and Master where rank and the preeminence of honors are concerned. We will recall, too, that we called both the golden altar and the compounded fine incense itself Christ, and said that Emmanuel himself is signified to us by both. Since, then, the incense points to Christ (for its fragrance is beyond compare), we will not make for ourselves incense like it. For we will accept no other at all besides him, as the wretched Jews indeed will: they will accept the son of lawlessness (John 5:43; 2 Thessalonians 2:3). For such people will be caught compounding for themselves an incense after the pattern of that fragrant and truly unique incense of God the Father, who has made manifest to us in the Son the fragrance of the knowledge of him (2 Corinthians 2:14). Through the Son we too give off a sweet fragrance (2 Corinthians 2:15), not because we have compounded the fine incense for ourselves, but because we share in the incense, have been anointed with the grace of the Spirit, and strive to win approval by the life we live in Christ.
Palladius: So it seems that through everything made in the holy tent the mystery of the Savior is given shape for us.
Cyril: And besides this you would be amazed to learn that even the craftsmen of the holy tent portray Christ, at least in their own persons.
Palladius: In what way do you mean? I cannot work it out.
Cyril: For it is written again: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe…’ (Exodus 31:1–2)

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-quotation: the word «Πατέρα» and «γάρ, φησί» close §30; the English here supplies 'father' so the verse reads whole, so §30's English should end at 'For he says:' without the word 'father' (or the overlap be trimmed at merge). Matthew 23:9 is quoted with the clause 'you are all brothers' from 23:8 joined to it, cited as 'Matthew 23:9, 8'. 'Any of the oil' renders ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, which refers back to the anointing oil of Exodus 30:33 discussed in §30. Incense recipe follows Cyril's LXX text of Exodus 30:34-38 (ἴσον ἴσῳ = 'an equal weight of each'; ὅθεν γνωσθήσομαί σοι ἐκεῖθεν = 'where I will make myself known to you'; Ἅγιον τῶν ἁγίων rendered 'most holy'). 'Beyond all natures' renders ἐπέκεινα ἁπασῶν (feminine plural, taken with φύσεων). Μεμνησόμεθα (future perfect) rendered 'we remember'. ἐπ' αὐτῷ taken as 'besides him' (could also be 'after him'). The clause about the Jews has no verb of its own; παραδέξονται is understood from παραδεξόμεθα, and τὸν τῆς ἀνομίας υἱόν is its object; this is Cyril's polemic, kept as written. 'Son of lawlessness': the closest New Testament wording is 2 Thessalonians 2:3 (ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, with 'son of destruction'); the idea of receiving 'another' echoes John 5:43; both cited as allusions. LXX Psalm 88:23 (English 89:22) has υἱὸς ἀνομίας but in a different sense, not cited. 'The fragrance of the knowledge of himself' follows 2 Corinthians 2:14 (τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ φανεροῦντι) with 2:15 (Χριστοῦ εὐωδία). Emmanuel used as a title (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23), not cited. 'Holy baptism' is Cyril's gloss, no citation. The section ends mid-word (φυ|λῆς) inside Exodus 31:2; §32 completes the quotation.
